Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test checks the chi-square statistic computed by ChiSquareTestImpl.chiSquare(double[] expected, long[] observed) method. The failure indicates that the statistic returned is incorrect for the given large values. 

Inspecting the implementation of chiSquare(double[], long[]) reveals that the method calculates the statistic by simply summing ((observed[i] - expected[i])^2 / expected[i]) for each category i. However, the current bug report states that this calculation is correct only when the sum of expected counts equals the sum of observed counts. This assumption is implicit but not enforced in the method. The provided test has large and differing sums of expected and observed arrays, likely violating this assumption.

This leads to an incorrect test statistic because the chi-square test statistic assumes that observed and expected totals are the same or the expected values have been scaled accordingly. The method currently does not adjust for cases when the total counts do not match. The failure is caused because the test passes raw expected counts while observed counts sum to a different value, but the method does not normalize or rescale expected counts to match the observed sum before calculating the chi-square.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this chi-square calculation issue and do not affect this diagnosis.

In conclusion, the root cause is that chiSquare() calculates the statistic without verifying or normalizing the sums of expected and observed arrays to be equal. This mismatch leads to an incorrect chi-square value returned.

Next, I can check if the class has a method for normalization or rescaling of expected counts or if the user/test is responsible for ensuring sums match.

Diagnosis summary:
The test calls ChiSquareTestImpl.chiSquare(double[] expected, long[] observed) with large expected and observed arrays. The method assumes the sums of expected and observed are equal, but this is not ensured. The chi-square statistic is computed by summing (observed[i] - expected[i])^2 / expected[i] directly, which is incorrect if the sums differ. This leads to the reported failure of incorrect test statistic.

The code does not perform any normalization to handle differing sums. It only verifies that all expected values are positive and all observed counts are non-negative.

Hence, the core bug is that the chiSquare method in ChiSquareTestImpl does not rescale expected counts to match observed counts when their sums differ, causing incorrect results when inputs violate this implicit assumption.

No relevant methods exist for sum normalization or rescaling, so either the method needs to be revised or the caller must ensure sums match.

Next, I suggest checks and revision in the chiSquare method to document or enforce this assumption or adjust input accordingly.

This concludes the fault diagnosis of the bug.
